catalogue.name: Legacy.Stock.List
catalogue.description: List stock reservations in Legacy App, all or by item filter, with count and total quantity (max 100 rows). Read-only. Gives the expectedCount for Legacy.Stock.ReleaseAll. For one item use Legacy.Stock.Get.
catalogue.selectionDescription: See the stock reservations in Legacy App, all or by item number filter, with their count and total quantity; at most 100 rows. Gives the count Legacy.Stock.ReleaseAll needs. For one item, use Legacy.Stock.Get; to release them, use Legacy.Stock.ReleaseAll.

subject.description: The reservations are selected by itemFilter in data.

target.description: Every reservation whose item number matches the filter. Empty or absent: all reservations.

parameters.name: itemFilter
parameters.description: A Business Central filter on the item number, at most 250 characters: 1896-S, 1896-S|1900-S or 19*. Empty or omitted: all reservations.

fields.name: itemFilter
fields.description: The filter used, as sent; empty for all.

fields.name: count
fields.description: The number of matching reservations, also when more is true. Send it to Legacy.Stock.ReleaseAll as expectedCount.

fields.name: totalQuantity
fields.description: The sum of the quantities of every matching reservation, also when more is true.

fields.name: returned
fields.description: The number of rows in reservations, at most 100.

fields.name: more
fields.description: true when count is larger than returned. Narrow the filter to see the rest.

fields.name: reservations
fields.description: One element per reservation, at most 100; empty when nothing matches.

errors.error: Parameter 'itemFilter' is '{filter}', which is not a valid filter: {reason} Send an item number or a filter such as 1896-S|1900-S or 19*.
errors.when: The filter syntax is invalid; {reason} is Business Central's own explanation.

errors.error: Parameter 'itemFilter' is {length} characters long; the maximum is 250.
Parameter 'itemFilter' must be a single value (text or number), not an object or an array.
errors.when: itemFilter is an object or an array.

errors.error: The request body must be a JSON object, with its parameters by name, for example { "name": "value" }.
errors.when: data is an array or plain text.
errors.fix: Send a JSON object, or no body at all.

preconditions: The caller can read Legacy Stock Reservation; without it the type is not offered.

related.name: Legacy.Stock.ReleaseAll
related.useInsteadWhen: The user agrees: release the reservations shown here.

steps.purpose: See which reservations the filter matches, and show the user what will be released.
When the user agrees: the same itemFilter, with the list's count as expectedCount.

workflow.text: Always list first. The release needs the list's count, so it cannot run on a selection nobody looked at. When the user already saw that count earlier in the conversation, send it directly: if anything changed since, the release is refused and nothing is released.

chapters.overview: Lists stock reservations in Legacy App, all or those whose item number matches a filter, with the count and the total quantity. At most 100 rows are returned; more is true when there are others. Read-only. Show the user the result before Legacy.Stock.ReleaseAll, which needs its count. Not for one item (use Legacy.Stock.Get).
chapters.notes: Safe to repeat: the same call gives the same answer until a reservation changes. count and totalQuantity always cover every matching reservation, even when only the first 100 rows are returned. Numbers use a dot as decimal separator. Error texts follow lcid when a translation is installed.

result.conventions:
## Errors and warnings
An error response has `status` = `Error`, a stable `code`, the `error` text and, when they apply, `parameter` (the request parameter concerned, e.g. `lines[2].no`), `received` (the value received), `expected` (what was expected) and `nextStep` (what to do now). `hint` says where to read more.
When a request has several problems, all of them are listed in `errors[]` - each with the same fields - under a top-level `code` (`MultipleErrors`, or a shared code such as `InvalidLine` for the `lines` of a Create type) and a summary `error`. Fix them all before calling again. One problem is reported at the top level, with no `errors[]`.
Request values are checked first and every problem found is reported together. A Business Central validation error raised afterwards, while a record is being written, stops the call and is reported on its own: `code` = `BusinessCentralError`, Business Central's own `error` text, and `parameter` naming the request parameter being applied, e.g. `lines[1].accountNo`. Nothing is written.
Request values are read in one format, whatever the language: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; date-times ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset; amounts as JSON numbers (or a string such as `"1234.56"`, no thousands separator); integers as JSON integers; booleans `true` or `false`. Any other value is `InvalidParameterFormat` with `received` and `expected`; for an unambiguous local form such as `26.09.2026`, `nextStep` gives the value to resend. Every bad value of a request is reported together.
Answers are written in one format as well, whatever the language of the call: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times ISO 8601, numbers with a dot and no thousands separator, and the option and enum values of every answer except `Data.Records.Get` and `Data.Records.Set` as their English names, so a value read from an answer can be sent back. Those two answer the caption of the language of the call, for a person to read. The language of the call (`lcid`) changes captions and message texts, not these forms. Two things are outside Bifrost's control: Business Central writes its own texts (a ledger entry description such as `Direct Cost V00010 on 10/02/26`, the text of a `BusinessCentralError`) with the regional settings of the server session, which `lcid` does not change, so a date in such a text can be in month-day order; and a table view is read with those settings too, so write dates in a view as `YYYY-MM-DD` and decimals with a dot.
Both success and error responses can carry `warnings[]`, each with `code`, `message` and, when they apply, `parameter` and `nextStep`.
`UnknownParameter` refuses undeclared data keys before execution for every type whose effect is not read, including a missing effect. The root envelope option `strict:false` cannot opt out. Read types keep warnings without changing status, validationResult or domain warningCount unless the caller sets `strict:true` (next to type and subject, never inside data). Refusals list the keys and localized nextStep corrections; no business changes or successful execution charges occur. Example: {"type":"Memory.User.Set","strict":true,"data":{"memory":"test","memry":"typo"}} is refused.
`FieldChangedByBC` is a warning from Data.Records.Set: another field validation or the write changed a sent field after its own validation. `parameter` names data[n].fields.{jsonName}, counting from 0. Status stays Success. Compare the returned values with what you sent; follow `nextStep` to use validation order or send the field again in a separate call. Normalisation of the field itself, LCY, Dimension Set ID, BLOB, Media, MediaSet and skipped fields are excluded.
Feature apps (Foundation 28.0.8 or later) can call `Argument.SetErrorContext(Parameter, Expected, NextStep)` before an operation that may fail after writes, then `Argument.ClearErrorContext()` after success. Supply the parameter name and translated labels, never request values, file content, credentials or a call stack. Foundation returns that context on the original `BusinessCentralError` after rollback, including uncaught task errors; `RespondWithLastError()` also uses it. The API does not catch errors, commit data or change the transaction boundary. Keep no-return `Codeunit.Run` and let errors propagate for chained `OmitCommit` calls; never add a Boolean `Codeunit.Run` or a writing `TryFunction` to recover context. Context is cleared between messages. Existing callers without context keep their response shape; recognized lock errors keep their existing `Retryable` guidance.
A message type that must run only one way (Foundation 28.0.9 or later) reads `Argument.GetInvocationSource()`: `Queue` when the task scheduler runs a message the queue API scheduled, `Task` for the Task API (`/tasks`), `Dispatcher` for an internal call through `Dispatcher ori` (the in-product MCP tool server, a nested dispatch from another message type), `Direct` for the Messages page Run Task action and anything unset. Only Foundation sets it; request values, parameters, source, subject and writes to the argument cannot change it. Refuse the other paths with `PreconditionFailed` and a `nextStep` that names the path to use.
`Retryable` means a transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. `error` keeps Business Central's original text. `expected` is "no concurrent lock on the same records"; `nextStep` is "Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed." Bifrost does not retry automatically. Uncaught recognized lock errors are also `Retryable` for `write` types. Uncaught `read` and `irreversible` errors remain `BusinessCentralError`, because an irreversible operation may already have committed.
`ConfirmationRequired` is the preview refusal for an irreversible type called without `expectedCount`. Nothing was changed; inspect `expected` and the description before sending the same request with that count. `ConfirmationMismatch` means the count has changed or the sent count was wrong; nothing was changed. Inspect the new preview before confirming again. Feature apps may implement `Msg Confirm ori` or call public `Confirm Gate ori.Confirm` to use the same protocol.
Codes: `MissingParameter`, `InvalidParameterFormat`, `InvalidParameter`, `RecordNotFound`, `AmbiguousRecord`, `ConflictingIdentifiers`, `InvalidFilterField`, `InvalidLine`, `NothingToPreview`, `LinesSkipped`, `BlockedByWriteGuard`, `PreconditionFailed`, `PermissionDenied`, `LimitExceeded`, `BusinessCentralError`, `MultipleErrors`, `DeprecatedParameter`, `UnknownParameter`, `FieldChangedByBC`, `Retryable`, `EULA_REQUIRED`, `TRIAL_NOT_STARTED`, `ConfirmationRequired`, `ConfirmationMismatch`. The `error` text may be translated; the code never is.
